markingScheme.criterion: Quotes two of their own jobs from the Investigation Record, each with the number of pieces (e.g. 'for 3 ÷ 1/4 I got 12 pieces').
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine jobs from the student's own Record with the correct piece count; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('I got lots of pieces') with no figures from their own jobs.

markingScheme.criterion: States the rule: dividing a whole number by a unit fraction (1/b) gives the same answer as multiplying the whole number by b (the denominator).
markingScheme.accept: 'n ÷ 1/b = n × b', 'multiply by the bottom number', or an equivalent example such as '3 ÷ 1/4 = 3 × 4'.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why there are more pieces: each whole is split into b equal pieces, so n wholes make n × b pieces (the pieces are smaller than 1, so more of them fit).
markingScheme.accept: Any reasoning that each whole makes b pieces, or that a fraction smaller than 1 fits into a whole more than once.
markingScheme.insufficient: Only saying 'because the pieces are small' without linking to each whole making b pieces.

markingScheme.criterion: Shows the multiplication used: 5 ÷ 1/3 = 5 × 3 (or each kilogram fills 3 bags, so 5 kg fills 5 × 3).
markingScheme.accept: 5 × 3 = 15, '3 bags from every kg', or a labelled diagram.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating 15 with no multiplication or method shown.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why the answer is bigger than 5: each bag holds less than 1 kg (1/3 kg), so every kilogram fills more than one bag.
markingScheme.accept: Any reasoning linking a bag size smaller than 1 kg (a fraction less than 1) to getting more bags than kilograms.
markingScheme.insufficient: Restating 'because 15 is bigger than 5' without a reason.
